claim.quote: For the first time, a detector achieves the directional measurement of proton and carbon recoils with kinetic energies in the keV range without any restriction on the direction of the incoming particle.

key_value.note: Angular resolution for proton recoils down to 4 keV kinetic energy (carbon: down to 5.5 keV).
key_value.quote: an angular resolution better than $16^\circ$ for proton recoils down to a kinetic energy of $4~\rm{keV}$

name: Directional detection of keV proton and carbon recoils with MIMAC

summary.plain: Exposing MIMAC to neutron beams, the team reconstructed the direction of proton and carbon recoils down to a few keV with an angular resolution better than 16 degrees.
summary.technical: Three neutron fields; angular resolution better than 16 deg for proton recoils down to 4 keV and carbon recoils down to 5.5 keV kinetic energy; directional reach towards O(1 GeV) WIMP masses.

title: Directional detection of keV proton and carbon recoils with MIMAC
why_it_matters: The abstract says this demonstrates that directional detection is around the corner for probing dark matter with masses down to O(1 GeV).
